description: A fungal disease caused by Venturia inaequalis that affects apple trees, causing dark, scaly lesions on leaves, fruits, and twigs.
symptoms:
• Olive-green to black spots on leaves
• Velvety, dark lesions on fruits
• Yellowing and premature leaf drop
• Cracked and deformed fruits
• Twig lesions and cankers
treatment:
• Apply fungicides like captan, myclobutanil, or sulfur
• Remove and destroy infected leaves and fruits
• Prune trees for better air circulation
• Use resistant apple varieties like Liberty or Freedom
• Apply dormant sprays in early spring
prevention:
• Plant resistant apple varieties
• Ensure proper tree spacing (15-20 feet apart)
• Clean up fallen leaves in autumn
• Avoid overhead watering
• Apply preventative fungicides before infection

description: A fungal disease caused by Podosphaera clandestina that creates white powdery growth on cherry leaves, shoots, and fruits.
symptoms:
• White powdery coating on leaves and shoots
• Curled and distorted leaves
• Stunted shoot growth
• Reduced fruit quality and size
• Premature leaf drop in severe cases
treatment:
• Apply sulfur or potassium bicarbonate sprays
• Use horticultural oils like neem oil
• Remove severely infected leaves
• Improve air circulation through pruning
• Apply fungicides at first sign of infection
prevention:
• Plant in sunny, well-ventilated locations
• Ensure good air circulation around trees
• Avoid overhead watering
• Use resistant cherry varieties
• Maintain proper tree spacing

description: A complex fungal disease caused by multiple pathogens that affects grapevines, leading to wood decay and various foliar symptoms.
symptoms:
• Tiger-stripe patterns on leaves
• Wood decay and cankers
• Reduced vine vigor
• Fruit spots and rotting
• Sudden vine collapse (apoplexy)
treatment:
• Prune infected wood below symptoms
• Protect pruning wounds with fungicides
• Remove severely infected vines
• Improve vineyard drainage
• Use balanced fertilization
prevention:
• Use certified disease-free planting material
• Proper pruning wound protection
• Avoid mechanical injuries to vines
• Maintain vine balance and health
• Regular vineyard monitoring
